hero.headline: Flock license plate cameras aid search for Vero Beach homicide person of interest
hero.teaser: The Indian River County Sheriff's Office is using a network of automated license plate cameras to search for Matthew Waggle, a person of interest in a Sunday homicide outside Vero Beach.
hero.body:
Indian River County Sheriff Eric Flowers took reporters inside the agency's Real Time Crime Center on Monday, where analysts are using Flock license plate cameras to search for 33-year-old Matthew Waggle. Waggle has not been charged but was identified as a person of interest after a 52-year-old woman was found shot near her home Sunday morning in the 500 block of First Street, just outside Vero Beach. Flowers said investigators believe the woman had been trying to end a relationship with Waggle and are investigating the killing as a domestic violence homicide.

Flock's automated license plate readers capture information about vehicles as they pass, including license plates, locations and timestamps. Indian River County operates 140 license plate readers. Flowers pointed to a deadly hit-and-run investigated by the Florida Highway Patrol last week as one recent example where analysts used Flock data to help build a case that otherwise had no leads.

Flowers defended the county's use of the cameras against growing national privacy concerns. He said law enforcement should be able to use available technology to protect the public. A nationwide BOLO has been issued for Waggle, who investigators say should be considered armed and dangerous and should not be approached.

cards.headline: Florida couple with full insurance and FEMA aid still unable to rebuild two years after 2024 hurricanes
cards.teaser: A Florida couple who carried both flood and homeowners insurance before the 2024 hurricane season received payments from their insurer and FEMA but remain on an empty lot nearly tw
cards.body:
A Florida couple who carried both flood and homeowners insurance before the 2024 hurricane season received payments from their insurer and FEMA but remain on an empty lot nearly two years later, unable to rebuild. Jen and RJ Garbowicz lost their home to flooding during Hurricane Helene in 2024, then sustained roof damage 13 days later during Hurricane Milton. The couple paid between $18,000 and $20,000 annually for both types of insurance.

The Garbowicz couple's flood insurance through FEMA's National Flood Insurance Program paid out the maximum of $250,000. Their mortgage holder is holding $200,000 of that payout, leaving the couple only $50,000 to rebuild. FEMA required the couple to rebuild under the 50% rule. After appealing four times by submitting the same documentation repeatedly, they received approval for a $33,000 FEMA disaster grant. The couple qualified for an SBA disaster loan but were told they must first cover the difference between insurance payments received and the total cost of rebuilding with their own cash. They also must repay the $33,000 FEMA grant before receiving the SBA loan.

Florida Emergency Management Director Kevin Guthrie, who served on the President's FEMA Review Council, told an insurance workshop in June that the average FEMA payout is $4,500. Guthrie urged insurance companies to ensure policyholders understand that FEMA will not make homeowners whole. The Garbowicz couple traveled to Washington, D.C., with the Extreme Weather Survivors group to advocate for the FEMA Act, a House proposal that would reform the agency. The bill would make FEMA an independent agency by removing it from the Department of Homeland Security, create a universal application process for disaster recovery, process FEMA grants faster by providing money to homeowners before recovery rather than as reimbursement, and facilitate investment in mitigation efforts and damage prevention before storms hit.

The couple estimates they have another 18 to 24 months of rebuilding ahead. RJ Garbowicz said the proposed reforms would have helped them rebuild sooner. Jennifer Garbowicz said getting their story out through interviews and putting pressure on lawmakers is what it will take to drive change. The couple remains in legal discussions with their homeowners insurance company over one claim.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie mayor's race tied to trash pickup problems ahead of primary
cards.teaser: Port St. Lucie Mayor Shannon Martin is facing two challengers who have attacked her leadership over the city's handling of garbage collection issues dating back to the pandemic.
cards.body:
Port St. Lucie Mayor Shannon Martin is fighting to hold on to her office as she faces two challengers, Steve Giordano and Eric Strazzeri, who have criticized her leadership over the city's handling of garbage collection issues. Dating back to the pandemic, trash has been a serious issue in the city and many residents say it's why the mayor's race is in the balance.

The city told residents they would be getting a tax credit, not a refund check in the mail, after the city won $24 million from a lawsuit against WastePro for years of shoddy service. Sometime later, the cost of trash collection went up. The question of how many times a week trash should be collected will be a ballot issue in November.

The mayor's race has also been overshadowed in recent days by a dispute over campaign signs that has led to a state investigation. Port St. Lucie police officers, including Mayor Shannon Martin's husband, Lt. Aaron Martin, were placed on paid administrative leave as the Florida Department of Law Enforcement took over a criminal investigation into two campaign-sign incidents involving mayoral challenger Steve Giordano. If there's a clear majority winner this week, the race will be decided, but if it's close, two finalists will advance to the General Election in November.

cards.headline: St. Lucie County population jumps 22% since 2020, adding more than 73,000 residents
cards.teaser: St. Lucie County's population reached 402,449 as of July 1, 2025, up from 329,226 in 2020, according to new Census estimates. Port St. Lucie now accounts for roughly two-thirds of the county's population.
cards.body:
St. Lucie County's population reached 402,449 as of July 1, 2025, up from 329,226 in 2020, according to Census Bureau estimates. That's an increase of more than 73,000 residents, or 22.2%, in just over five years. For comparison, neighboring Palm Beach County grew from 1,492,191 residents in 2020 to an estimated 1,575,726 in 2025, an increase of about 5.6%. St. Lucie County has grown at roughly four times the rate of Palm Beach County since 2020.

Much of St. Lucie County's population is concentrated in Port St. Lucie. The Census Bureau estimates 268,062 people now live in Port St. Lucie, meaning the city accounts for roughly two-thirds of the county's entire population. Port St. Lucie has also grown faster than the county overall. The city's population is up nearly 31% from its 2020 estimates base of 204,826.

Jason Coley with Atlantic Shores Realty, Expertise ERA Powered, said affordability remains one of the biggest factors he sees among his clients. According to Coley, a buyer spending between $400,000 and $500,000 in St. Lucie County can find a four-bedroom, two-bathroom home with a two-car garage on a quarter-acre lot. He estimated a comparable newer home in Palm Beach County could cost between $600,000 and $800,000. Coley said some of his clients are willing to make a longer commute, while others are able to work remotely.

cards.headline: Kuhio Aloy hits first two pro homers as St. Lucie Mets fall 7-3 to Jupiter
cards.teaser: Kuhio Aloy hit the first two home runs of his professional career Sunday, but the St. Lucie Mets fell 7-3 to the Jupiter Hammerheads to close out a difficult road series.
cards.body:
Kuhio Aloy hit the first two home runs of his professional career Sunday, but the St. Lucie Mets could not overcome a late surge by the Jupiter Hammerheads in a 7-3 loss at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium.

The defeat ended a difficult six-game series for St. Lucie, with Jupiter winning five of the six games. The Mets have now lost seven of their last eight.

Aloy, the Mets' 11th-round pick out of Arkansas, provided the offensive highlight for St. Lucie with a pair of solo home runs.

His first came in the second inning and gave the Mets a 1-0 lead. Aloy went deep again in the sixth, tying the game 2-2.

Jupiter slugger Echedry Vargas answered with another big performance of his own. Vargas hit a two-run homer off Candido Cuevas in the fourth inning to put the Hammerheads ahead 2-1.

After Aloy tied the game in the top of the sixth, Vargas responded in the bottom half with a towering solo home run off Conner Ware, putting Jupiter back in front 3-2.

It was Vargas' second multi-homer game of the series. He finished the six-game set with five home runs and now leads the Florida State League with 21 this season. Vargas is the first Hammerheads player to reach at least 20 home runs in a season since Marcell Ozuna in 2012.

Jupiter pulled away with three runs in the seventh inning. One run scored on a groundout and another came home on an error before Jeremy Almonte delivered an RBI double off Jose Guevara, stretching the Hammerheads' lead to 6-2.

The Mets attempted to rally in the ninth after Jupiter reliever Ian Medina walked four batters. Elian Peña drew a bases-loaded walk to force home a run and cut the deficit to 7-3.

Davidxon Lara then entered for Jupiter and retired John Smith III on a groundout with the tying run at the plate to end the game.

Mets starter Will Watson, who is working his way back from an oblique injury on a Minor League Baseball rehab assignment, pitched three scoreless innings.

St. Lucie finished the day at 17-30 in the second half and 50-63 overall.

The Mets are off Monday before returning home Tuesday to begin a six-game series against the Lakeland Flying Tigers at Clover Park in Port St. Lucie. First pitch for Tuesday's opener is scheduled for 6:10 p.m.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie police rescue ducklings trapped in storm drain on Southeast Oakridge Drive
cards.teaser: Officers Ortiz and Garcia responded Friday to Southeast Oakridge Drive and Southeast Oaklyn Street, where young ducks had fallen into a storm drain.
cards.body:
Port St. Lucie Police Department Officers Ortiz and Garcia responded Friday to the area of Southeast Oakridge Drive and Southeast Oaklyn Street, where a group of ducklings had fallen into a storm drain. Body camera video released by the department shows officers working around the storm drain and reaching inside to retrieve the ducklings one by one. Their mother remained nearby as officers worked to free her babies.

After carefully removing the ducklings from the drain, officers reunited them with their mother, bringing the call to a happy ending. The department wrote in a Facebook post that protecting the community can sometimes include its smallest residents. The department said it is always there to lend a helping hand, especially when the smallest community members need assistance.

cards.headline: Kuhio Aloy hits first two pro homers as St. Lucie Mets fall 7-3 to Jupiter
cards.teaser: Kuhio Aloy hit the first two home runs of his professional career Sunday, but the St. Lucie Mets fell 7-3 to the Jupiter Hammerheads to close out a difficult road series.
cards.body:
Kuhio Aloy hit the first two home runs of his professional career Sunday, but the St. Lucie Mets could not overcome a late surge by the Jupiter Hammerheads in a 7-3 loss at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium.

The defeat ended a difficult six-game series for St. Lucie, with Jupiter winning five of the six games. The Mets have now lost seven of their last eight.

Aloy, the Mets' 11th-round pick out of Arkansas, provided the offensive highlight for St. Lucie with a pair of solo home runs.

His first came in the second inning and gave the Mets a 1-0 lead. Aloy went deep again in the sixth, tying the game 2-2.

Jupiter slugger Echedry Vargas answered with another big performance of his own. Vargas hit a two-run homer off Candido Cuevas in the fourth inning to put the Hammerheads ahead 2-1.

After Aloy tied the game in the top of the sixth, Vargas responded in the bottom half with a towering solo home run off Conner Ware, putting Jupiter back in front 3-2.

It was Vargas' second multi-homer game of the series. He finished the six-game set with five home runs and now leads the Florida State League with 21 this season. Vargas is the first Hammerheads player to reach at least 20 home runs in a season since Marcell Ozuna in 2012.

Jupiter pulled away with three runs in the seventh inning. One run scored on a groundout and another came home on an error before Jeremy Almonte delivered an RBI double off Jose Guevara, stretching the Hammerheads' lead to 6-2.

The Mets attempted to rally in the ninth after Jupiter reliever Ian Medina walked four batters. Elian Peña drew a bases-loaded walk to force home a run and cut the deficit to 7-3.

Davidxon Lara then entered for Jupiter and retired John Smith III on a groundout with the tying run at the plate to end the game.

Mets starter Will Watson, who is working his way back from an oblique injury on a Minor League Baseball rehab assignment, pitched three scoreless innings.

St. Lucie finished the day at 17-30 in the second half and 50-63 overall.

The Mets are off Monday before returning home Tuesday to begin a six-game series against the Lakeland Flying Tigers at Clover Park in Port St. Lucie. First pitch for Tuesday's opener is scheduled for 6:10 p.m.

hero.headline: St. Lucie County population jumps 22% since 2020, adding more than 73,000 residents
hero.teaser: St. Lucie County's population reached 402,449 as of July 1, 2025, up from 329,226 in 2020, according to new Census estimates. Port St. Lucie now accounts for roughly two-thirds of the county's population.
hero.body:
St. Lucie County's population reached 402,449 as of July 1, 2025, up from 329,226 in 2020, according to Census Bureau estimates. That's an increase of more than 73,000 residents, or 22.2%, in just over five years. For comparison, neighboring Palm Beach County grew from 1,492,191 residents in 2020 to an estimated 1,575,726 in 2025, an increase of about 5.6%. St. Lucie County has grown at roughly four times the rate of Palm Beach County since 2020.

Much of St. Lucie County's population is concentrated in Port St. Lucie. The Census Bureau estimates 268,062 people now live in Port St. Lucie, meaning the city accounts for roughly two-thirds of the county's entire population. Port St. Lucie has also grown faster than the county overall. The city's population is up nearly 31% from its 2020 estimates base of 204,826.

Jason Coley with Atlantic Shores Realty, Expertise ERA Powered, said affordability remains one of the biggest factors he sees among his clients. According to Coley, a buyer spending between $400,000 and $500,000 in St. Lucie County can find a four-bedroom, two-bathroom home with a two-car garage on a quarter-acre lot. He estimated a comparable newer home in Palm Beach County could cost between $600,000 and $800,000. Coley said some of his clients are willing to make a longer commute, while others are able to work remotely.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie mayor's race tied to trash pickup problems ahead of primary
cards.teaser: Port St. Lucie Mayor Shannon Martin is facing two challengers who have attacked her leadership over the city's handling of garbage collection issues dating back to the pandemic.
cards.body:
Port St. Lucie Mayor Shannon Martin is fighting to hold on to her office as she faces two challengers, Steve Giordano and Eric Strazzeri, who have criticized her leadership over the city's handling of garbage collection issues. Dating back to the pandemic, trash has been a serious issue in the city and many residents say it's why the mayor's race is in the balance.

The city told residents they would be getting a tax credit, not a refund check in the mail, after the city won $24 million from a lawsuit against WastePro for years of shoddy service. Sometime later, the cost of trash collection went up. The question of how many times a week trash should be collected will be a ballot issue in November.

The mayor's race has also been overshadowed in recent days by a dispute over campaign signs that has led to a state investigation. Port St. Lucie police officers, including Mayor Shannon Martin's husband, Lt. Aaron Martin, were placed on paid administrative leave as the Florida Department of Law Enforcement took over a criminal investigation into two campaign-sign incidents involving mayoral challenger Steve Giordano. If there's a clear majority winner this week, the race will be decided, but if it's close, two finalists will advance to the General Election in November.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie police rescue ducklings trapped in storm drain on Southeast Oakridge Drive
cards.teaser: Officers Ortiz and Garcia responded Friday to Southeast Oakridge Drive and Southeast Oaklyn Street, where young ducks had fallen into a storm drain.
cards.body:
Port St. Lucie Police Department Officers Ortiz and Garcia responded Friday to the area of Southeast Oakridge Drive and Southeast Oaklyn Street, where a group of ducklings had fallen into a storm drain. Body camera video released by the department shows officers working around the storm drain and reaching inside to retrieve the ducklings one by one. Their mother remained nearby as officers worked to free her babies.

After carefully removing the ducklings from the drain, officers reunited them with their mother, bringing the call to a happy ending. The department wrote in a Facebook post that protecting the community can sometimes include its smallest residents. The department said it is always there to lend a helping hand, especially when the smallest community members need assistance.

hero.headline: Flock license plate cameras aid search for Vero Beach homicide person of interest
hero.teaser: The Indian River County Sheriff's Office is using a network of automated license plate cameras to search for Matthew Waggle, a person of interest in a Sunday homicide outside Vero Beach.
hero.body:
Indian River County Sheriff Eric Flowers took reporters inside the agency's Real Time Crime Center on Monday, where analysts are using Flock license plate cameras to search for 33-year-old Matthew Waggle. Waggle has not been charged but was identified as a person of interest after a 52-year-old woman was found shot near her home Sunday morning in the 500 block of First Street, just outside Vero Beach. Flowers said investigators believe the woman had been trying to end a relationship with Waggle and are investigating the killing as a domestic violence homicide.

Flock's automated license plate readers capture information about vehicles as they pass, including license plates, locations and timestamps. Indian River County operates 140 license plate readers. Flowers pointed to a deadly hit-and-run investigated by the Florida Highway Patrol last week as one recent example where analysts used Flock data to help build a case that otherwise had no leads.

Flowers defended the county's use of the cameras against growing national privacy concerns. He said law enforcement should be able to use available technology to protect the public. A nationwide BOLO has been issued for Waggle, who investigators say should be considered armed and dangerous and should not be approached.
